notes: Minor definitional difference, not an error: execute_summary.json's 'multi_label_sum' 10214 sums all 7 buckets including 'other'; the named-category multi-label sum is 5975 (5975 + 4239 = 10214).
'other' is the largest bucket (4239 = 46.7% of negative tweets), so named-category volumes are lower bounds on true complaint counts; this is disclosed in upstream artifacts rather than hidden.

Keyword matching is substring-based per the task spec, so tokens such as 'wait', 'hours', 'bag' and 'late' also fire in unrelated contexts (word-boundary matching would give delay 1964 / service 1093 / baggage 869 / seat 239 / food 95 / other 4785 per data_profile.json sensitivity).
Virgin America has only 504 tweets (181 negative), so its percentages carry low precision and should not be over-interpreted.
No row filtering was required: the source data has no missing airline/sentiment/text values, so there is no silent data loss between source and outputs.
conclusion: Both deliverables are structurally valid, complete, and numerically reproducible from the source database (0 mismatches across 60 verified data cells); no corrections needed.
